# generator-shortcuts — executable counterexample

## Rival: always complete all four border corners

The strongest **verified plausible rival I found** is `complete_all_corners`: do the
intended orientation-to-border transformation for observed L triominoes, then fill
all otherwise missing output corners with the smallest foreground color. It fits
all four canonical pairs because every canonical input contains all four
orientations. “Strongest” here means strongest among the concrete rivals checked,
not a proof over every possible shortcut.

## Exact emitted disagreement

Final generator SHA-256: `14f3c3a81127c7f65da3bd837ef287021fb5d8cba1c61f65dc76ac8d5c8af384`.
Request: `generate(0, 0, canvas_size=7, bg_color=8, n_corners=1, palette_size=1)`.
`self_check` returns `[]`.

Input:

```text
8888855
8888885
8888888
8888888
8888888
8888888
8888888
```

Canonical Racket output:

```text
8888555
8888885
8888885
8888888
8888888
8888888
8888888
```

Rival output:

```text
5558555
5888885
5888885
8888888
5888885
5888885
5558555
```

Only the observed upper-right orientation is enlarged by the intended rule; the
other three corners remain background. The rival fills those absent corners.

## Verification and generator coverage

`checks/main-shortcut-final.json` records five source-bound cases: this generated
witness plus all four canonical pairs. The protected Racket runtime agreed with
the expected output on all five, and the rival disagreed only on the generated
witness. Exact rule SHA-256: `c83accbef454499a8c9af94eaf34ddd2d50551e7312ed9a0360c34a00985fd89`.

The generator emits this exact witness under the request above. Its default
four-slot schedule contains two incomplete and two complete orientation sets in
each difficulty band, so every three-demonstration holdout contains at least one
case that refutes this rival. The retained 300-lesson census found zero ambiguity
in 1,200 query rotations; this is finite declared-rival evidence, not universal
identifiability proof.
